stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis. Its velocity at time t seconds is \( v(t) = t^{3} + 4 t^{2} - 4 t - 58 \) meters per second, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the speed of the particle at time t = 3, and determine whether the speed is increasing or decreasing at that time. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The speed is 7 meters per second, and it is decreasing at that time, because \( v(3) = -7 \) and \( a(3) = 47 \) have opposite signs.

worked_solution.text: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, \( a(t) = 3 t^{2} + 8 t - 4 \), so \( a(3) = 47 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: acceleration is the derivative of velocity

worked_solution.text: The speed is \( \left|v(3)\right| = 7 \) meters per second.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed is the absolute value of velocity

worked_solution.text: Because \( v(3) = -7 \) and \( a(3) = 47 \) have opposite signs, the speed of the particle is decreasing at t = 3.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed increases when velocity and acceleration share a sign

options.label: The speed is 7 meters per second, and it is increasing at that time, because \( a(3) = 47 \) is positive, so the particle is speeding up.
options.derivation: the change in speed decided from the sign of the acceleration alone, without the sign of the velocity
